title: In the Living Room
cardDescription: Seats, soft furnishings, and familiar living-room objects.
description: Make yourself comfortable with a crossword about the seats, soft furnishings, and everyday objects found in a living room.
focus: This puzzle looks at furniture and furnishings around a sitting area. Clues distinguish the whole item from one of its parts or a smaller accessory. Some familiar words have other meanings elsewhere, so the living-room setting helps point to the intended answer.
solvingTip: Look for the object's job: supporting a person, protecting a table from a glass, displaying flowers, or covering a window. A furnishing and its small accessory can have different names. Start with a familiar short object to help cross into a longer furniture word.
words: Long upholstered seat for more than one person
A seat designed for one person
Soft padded support placed on a seat
A movable light used for reading or lighting a room
A floor covering that does not usually cover the entire room
Fabric panel hung at a window
Window covering with slats or a roll-up surface
A hanging fabric window covering, often heavier than a sheer panel
Furniture with a flat top supported above the floor
Small mat placed beneath a drinking glass
Padded footrest that may also provide extra seating
Low piece of furniture used to support the feet
Handheld control used to change a television channel
Surface on which a television picture appears
An object that displays the time of day
Container used to display cut flowers
Floor area at the base of a fireplace
Built-in place in a room where a contained fire may burn
Bordered holder around a photograph or picture

answerNotes.COASTER: Coaster means the small protective mat under a drink here. It can also name an amusement-park ride, but the reference to a glass fixes the household meaning.
answerNotes.OTTOMAN: An ottoman is a padded footrest or low seat. Some versions have storage inside, but that extra feature is not required by the clue.
answerNotes.MANTEL: Mantel names the structure above a fireplace. Mantle is a different spelling with other meanings, so the location and ending letters both help.
answerNotes.HEARTH: The hearth is at the base of a fireplace, while the mantel is above it. The positional word in the clue distinguishes two related features.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp is the lighting device, not just the bulb inside it. The clue describes a movable room light rather than the electrical part alone.
answerNotes.RUG: A rug commonly covers part of a floor. Carpet often describes a larger installed covering, although everyday use of the words can overlap.

title: Tools at the Kitchen Counter
cardDescription: Utensils for mixing, serving, peeling, and draining.
description: Find familiar kitchen utensils through clear clues about everyday jobs, from peeling a vegetable to serving soup.
focus: The answers name utensils and cookware rather than foods or recipe quantities. Most clues describe the task an item performs, while partial phrases identify familiar kitchen tools. Similar-looking tools can have different jobs, so pay attention to the action in each clue.
solvingTip: Identify the job before choosing a tool: mixing, lifting, peeling, or separating. A deep serving tool is different from a wire-loop mixing tool. Short cookware names can give you a foothold among the longer utensil names.
words: Cutting utensil with a sharpened blade
Eating or stirring utensil with a small rounded bowl
Eating utensil with several pointed tines
Wire-loop tool used to beat eggs or blend ingredients
Deep-bowled utensil used to serve soup
Flat tool commonly used to lift or turn food in a pan
Paired gripping arms used to lift or hold food
Tool used to remove the thin outer skin of a vegetable
Perforated tool used to shred cheese or vegetables
Bowl with drainage holes, often used for pasta
Tea ___: a mesh tool that catches loose leaves
Cutting ___: a surface used for chopping food
Protective covering tied over clothing while cooking
Oven ___: padded hand covering for handling hot cookware
Shallow cooking vessel often used for frying
Deep cooking vessel commonly used for soup or boiling water
Rounded open container used for mixing or serving
Removable cover for a cooking vessel
Fine-mesh tool used to sift flour or separate small particles
Potato ___: a handled tool for crushing cooked potatoes

answerNotes.LADLE: A ladle has a deep bowl for transferring liquids such as soup. That shape separates it from the flatter tool described by a turning or lifting clue.
answerNotes.COLANDER: A colander is usually a bowl-shaped draining vessel with holes. A fine-mesh strainer or sieve may catch smaller particles, so the clue's shape and task matter.
answerNotes.SPATULA: Spatula is used for several kitchen tools. Here, the clue describes the flat lifting or turning kind rather than a flexible scraper for the side of a bowl.
answerNotes.TONGS: Tongs grip food between two arms. The plural-looking word names one utensil, which is why the clue describes paired arms rather than two separate tools.
answerNotes.SIEVE: A sieve uses a screen or mesh to separate material by particle size. The flour-sifting example helps distinguish its task from draining a large pot of pasta.
answerNotes.PEELER: A peeler removes a thin outer layer. A grater makes shreds, so the two tools are not interchangeable in the wording of these clues.

title: Laundry Day Words
cardDescription: Clothing, wash-cycle words, and familiar laundry equipment.
description: Work through a gentle crossword about clothing and the familiar words used around a washer, dryer, and laundry basket.
focus: This puzzle combines laundry objects with the words for common stages of washing and finishing clothes. Some answers name equipment, some describe an action, and others identify a fabric item or something removed from it. The clues explain the intended everyday meaning.
solvingTip: Decide whether the clue asks for a machine, an action, or a piece of clothing. A complete program and one rinsing or spinning stage have different names. Short action words can help you cross into the longer equipment names.
words: Machine that cleans clothing in water
Machine that removes moisture from laundry
Open container used to carry a load of laundry
Laundry container whose name also means hinder
Cleaning product commonly added to a washing machine
Cleaning material traditionally made from fats and an alkali
Wash away remaining cleaning product with water
Turn rapidly to extract water in a washing-machine stage
A complete programmed sequence of washing-machine stages
Small loose fibers shed from fabrics
Absorbent cloth used for drying the body or hands
Large piece of fabric used as a covering on a bed
A foot covering worn inside a shoe
An upper-body garment commonly having sleeves
A discolored mark left on fabric
Clip used to hold washing on a line
Heated appliance used to smooth wrinkles in fabric
Water vapor that may come from a clothes-pressing appliance
Whitening agent sometimes used in laundering
Bend fabric over itself to make a neater, smaller shape

answerNotes.LINT: Lint consists of small fibers released from fabric. A stain is a mark or discoloration, so the clue's description of fibers points to a different answer.
answerNotes.RINSE: Rinse names the stage that uses water to remove remaining cleaning product. Spin names a different action, using rapid rotation to help remove water.
answerNotes.CYCLE: A cycle is the whole programmed sequence. An individual rinse or spin stage can be part of that sequence rather than another name for the entire cycle.
answerNotes.IRON: Iron is the appliance in this household context. The word can also name a metal, but the reference to pressing fabric selects the appliance meaning.
answerNotes.HAMPER: Hamper is a container in this clue. It also has a verb meaning to hinder, which does not fit the reference to collecting clothes.
answerNotes.CLOTHESPIN: Clothespin is the familiar American word for the clip that holds washing on a line. Clothes peg is common in British English for the same object.

title: At the Front Door
cardDescription: Doors, steps, and the familiar details of a home's entrance.
description: Picture an entrance and solve familiar clues about door fittings, porch features, and the path that leads up to a home.
focus: The answers concern the entrance area and nearby fittings. Clues distinguish an opening from its hardware and a walking surface from a support beside it. Several short household words have other meanings elsewhere, so the location described is part of the clue.
solvingTip: Notice whether the clue describes an opening, a signal, a place to stand, or something held for support. A door panel and the key used with its lock have different jobs. Short partial phrases can help connect the longer entrance-area words.
words: Movable panel used to close an entrance to a room or building
Small item cut to fit and operate a particular lock
Mechanism that secures a door and may be opened with a key
Door fastener whose name rhymes with catch
Rounded door handle turned by hand
Part grasped to pull or push a door
Joint that lets a door swing open or closed
Device pressed by a visitor to sound a signal inside a home
Covered outdoor space attached to a house, often near its entrance
Small platform or group of steps just outside an entrance
Door ___: a covering on which shoes can be wiped
One level foothold in a flight of stairs
One of the ascending steps connecting building levels
Hand___: a support grasped beside steps
Container where a household receives delivered letters
Narrow opening through which letters can be pushed
Movable opening panel in a fence
A narrow way leading toward a doorway
Foldable canopy carried to keep rain off a person
A ringing tone that may announce a visitor

answerNotes.STOOP: Stoop can name the platform or steps outside an entrance. It also means to bend the body, but the doorway context selects the structure.
answerNotes.HINGE: A hinge allows the door to pivot. A handle is grasped, and a latch holds the door closed; the different jobs help distinguish these hardware terms.
answerNotes.GATE: Gate here means an opening panel in a fence. At an airport the word can name a boarding area, but the home-entrance clue specifies the fence meaning.
answerNotes.RAIL: Handrail is often written as one word, but the partial phrase supplies hand and asks you to fill the remaining part. The intended object is a support beside steps.
answerNotes.LATCH: Latch rhymes with catch, which supplies a spelling hint alongside the door-fastener meaning. The clue does not ask for the key-operated security mechanism.
answerNotes.KNOB: A knob is a rounded kind of handle. Other handles may have levers or pulls, so the clue uses the shape to narrow the intended word.

title: A Place for Everything
cardDescription: Shelves, drawers, and the parts of everyday storage.
description: Enjoy a small organizing-themed crossword about storage furniture, compartments, and the containers that keep belongings together.
focus: This puzzle follows where household objects are kept and how they are grouped. A whole cabinet, a pull-out compartment, and a single horizontal support are different answers. One short action word describes putting things away, while the object clues describe the storage itself.
solvingTip: Notice whether a clue names the whole storage unit, a pull-out part, or a lining. A paired set and a bundle describe groups of items, while a container is the object holding them. The word indicating an action asks you to put things away.
words: Horizontal board used to support stored or displayed objects
Pull-out compartment in a piece of furniture
Storage furniture with doors and enclosed compartments
Small built-in space used to store clothing or household items
Shaped support on which a garment is hung
Open container used to hold or sort objects
Container commonly made of cardboard with flat sides
Storage container often opened by lifting a hinged top
Small open compartment for storing personal belongings
Partition used to keep groups of objects apart
Tag or marking that identifies the contents of a container
Material placed inside a drawer to cover its bottom
Arrange items into groups by type or another shared feature
A matched set of two, such as two shoes
Folded cover used to keep papers together
A collection of papers kept together for reference
A group of items tied or wrapped together
Put items away in a suitable storage place

answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer is the sliding compartment, not the entire cabinet or dresser. The pull-out movement in the clue identifies that particular part.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is one horizontal support. Shelving or a cabinet can include several of them, so a clue asking for one board takes the singular answer.
answerNotes.LINER: A liner covers the inside surface of something. In this clue it is material at the bottom of a drawer, not a person or a whole storage container.
answerNotes.PAIR: Pair names two things considered together. It sounds like pear, the fruit, but the reference to matching shoes selects the quantity meaning.
answerNotes.CLOSET: A closet is an enclosed storage space, often built into a room. A cabinet is a piece of storage furniture; the clue's reference to a built-in space helps distinguish them.
answerNotes.SORT: Sort is used as a verb meaning to arrange things by a shared feature. It does not mean a type or kind, which is another everyday use of the word.
